newsitem.title: LATVIA: CABINET OKAYS CHANGES TO BUDGET.
newsitem.headline: CABINET OKAYS CHANGES TO BUDGET.

text.p: Latvia's cabinet has approved amendments to the 1997 state budget, increasing it by some 35 million lats but keeping it balanced, the finance ministry said on Tuesday.

In accordance to the amendments, which still have to be approved by parliament, revenue and expenditure in the overall state budget will be increased by 35 million lats and by 19 million lats in the central government budget.

"I highly appreciate the government's ability to balance revenue and expenditure...while keeping the budget balanced on the path towards economic stability," Finance Minister Robert Zile was quoted as saying in a statement.
The changes are in response by to conservative revenue forecasts which have been outperformed and by politically motivated tax forecasts which did not occur, the ministry said.

Increases in expenditure will be covered by an additional nine million lats from the state privatisation fund, an increase in the excise tax on strong spirits as well as redistributing the existing expenditure plans.
The government also plans to increase the excise tax by 0.5 percent on one litre of pure alcohol and sees 1.46 million lats flowing into the state coffers as a result.
The money is to be used for transport subsidies to the disabled.
The cabinet has proposed that 5.2 million lats from six million lats earlier earmarked for the construction of a prison be diverted for, among other things, payment reform in the military.
